corrections.title: fused-memory MCP calls fail within a second with the harness's `Unable to connect` while fused-memory.service restarts with port 8002 unbound -- not a backing-store timeout and not worktree-specific
corrections.cause: Port 8002 was CLOSED: the watchdog's liveness revive restarted fused-memory.service with the old stop/start path, which left 8002 unbound until `Started`, so each connect was refused and the harness's MCP HTTP client reported `Unable to connect. Is the computer able to access the url?` within a second. Measured 2026-09-19 (BST) from `journalctl --user -u fused-memory.service` and `-u orchestrator-watchdog.service`: 19:26:54 watchdog liveness verdict 'wedged' (streak 3/3) and systemd `Stopping`; 19:27:41 SIGTERM serviced; 19:27:50 the session's last successful fused-memory call (a search) answered; 19:27:56 `Consumed` then `Starting`, with no `Stopped` line; 19:28:07 and 19:28:17 the two failed add_memory calls, returning in 0.3s and 0.7s; 19:28:36 `Started` -- both failures inside the 40s start. The request never reached the server process, so no backing store was involved, and 8002 is host-global, so nothing about it is worktree-specific. Since 2026-09-29 socket activation (commits 8ac33458c4, a1548f5c64, b481d598aa) holds 8002 in fused-memory.socket across a restart, a watchdog revive (now `reset-failed` + `restart --no-block`, never `stop`) or a crash, so a mid-restart client waits in the kernel backlog instead of being refused. The port still closes on a deliberate `systemctl --user stop`/`disable` of fused-memory.service (its ExecStopPost stops the socket), on the port-change stop-then-start in scripts/setup-host.sh section 4, and on a host where fused-memory.socket is not installed. scripts/fm_wedge_forensics.py measures such an episode's stall, teardown and startup from a `journalctl --user -u fused-memory.service -o short-iso` capture.
corrections.note: CORRECTION (task 5688). This entry's prior title -- "add_memory fails twice with an opaque connectivity error inside a task worktree, threatening loss of a verified finding" -- and its founding candidate's cause (cand-20260919-3: "no indication of which backing store timed out", "no retry/backoff or local fallback path to preserve the finding") carry three framings, all WITHDRAWN as refuted by the journal: (1) not worktree-specific -- port 8002 is host-global and every client's .mcp.json points at it; (2) no backing store timed out -- the request never reached the server process; (3) nothing was at risk of loss -- the payload never left the client, and the string is emitted by the harness's MCP HTTP client, so no retry/backoff is implementable in this repository. Call times were read from the founding session's own transcript (archived at data/orchestrator/agent-transcripts/5650/), journal times from `journalctl --user`. Status set to fixed because landed, deployed changes removed the cause, verified first-hand 2026-10-09: `systemctl --user is-active`/`is-enabled fused-memory.socket` = active/enabled; `systemctl --user show fused-memory.service -p TriggeredBy` = `TriggeredBy=fused-memory.socket`; the socket's journal ends at `Listening on fused-memory.socket` 2026-09-29 23:13:51 with no close since. A recurrence of `Unable to connect` from fused-memory after 2026-09-29 means a deliberate stop/disable, the port-change path, or a missing socket: check `TriggeredBy` and the socket's journal for `Closed fused-memory.socket` before reopening. This ANNOTATES rather than retracts the existing sightings. The 2026-09-20 sighting (session ae321fc6-719d-419f-aee0-6aa233f712d8, archived at data/orchestrator/agent-transcripts/5238/) was checked against the journal and is a DIFFERENT mechanism, measured: its add_memory was issued 23:42:11 BST and failed at 23:43:41 with `The operation timed out.` -- not `Unable to connect`, and not a connectivity error -- entirely inside a 183s self-recovered event-loop stall (fused-memory's journal silent 23:41:21 -> 23:44:24 with no systemd lifecycle line; orchestrator-watchdog logged liveness verdict 'wedged' streak 1/3 at 23:42:25 and 2/3 at 23:43:26, and never restarted it). The port stayed bound throughout, so socket activation does NOT fix that sighting's cause; it shares its harness string with pending cand-20260909-11. The four pending candidates carrying this entry's `Unable to connect` string (cand-20260730-13, cand-20260802-5, cand-20260805-2, cand-20260910-4) and cand-20260909-11 are NOT adjudicated here: disposition is census-owned.
